findings.evidence:
`Create your Meridian Outfitters account` but `

Create your account

`
findings.fix: Change the `<h1>` to "Create your Meridian Outfitters account" (or otherwise make title and heading consistent).
findings.violation: The page title includes the brand name but the visible heading drops it, so the two don't match and the user loses the brand confirmation on the page itself.

findings.evidence: `<input id="password-input" ... minlength="8" required="">` with no visible helper text
findings.fix: Add visible helper text under the password field, e.g. "Must be at least 8 characters."
findings.violation: The 8-character minimum is enforced only via the `minlength` attribute; nothing in the visible UI tells the user the requirement before they get a validation error.

findings.fix: Add `minlength="8"` to the confirm-password input to match the password field.
findings.violation: Unlike the password field, this input has no `minlength="8"`, so the two related fields have inconsistent validation constraints.
"e-mail" is not a valid HTML autocomplete token (the correct value is "email"), so browsers won't recognize it and autofill for this field will silently fail.

findings.fix: Differentiate them, e.g. keep `tel` for the primary and use `autocomplete="tel-national"`/a distinct section token or just remove autocomplete from the secondary field.
findings.violation: Using the identical autocomplete token for two different phone fields can cause the browser to autofill the same stored number into both the primary and secondary phone fields.

findings.fix: Make the website field optional, or remove it unless this form is specifically for business accounts.
findings.violation: Requiring a company website on a consumer outfitters account-signup form is unnecessary friction - most individual shoppers don't have one, and nothing else on the form explains why it's needed.

findings.evidence: `<input id="member-input" ... placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">` with no `maxlength` or `pattern`
findings.fix: Add `pattern="\d{8}"` and `maxlength="8"`, and move the "Must be 8 digits" instruction into visible helper text instead of (or in addition to) the placeholder.
findings.violation: The "8 digits" requirement is communicated only through placeholder text, which disappears once the user starts typing, and there is no `pattern`/`maxlength` to actually enforce 8 digits.

findings.fix: Rename the label or add helper text clarifying what "account number" refers to (or remove the field if it duplicates "Membership number").
findings.violation: "Account number" is ambiguous in context - it's unclear whether this refers to a Meridian Outfitters account, a bank account, or something else, and no helper text clarifies it.

findings.evidence: Street address (`row-street`) is followed by `row-phone`, `row-phone2`, `row-website`, `row-member`, `row-acctnum` before `row-postal` (postal code) appears
findings.fix: Move `row-postal` directly after `row-street` so all address fields are contiguous.
findings.violation: The postal code is separated from the other address fields (house number, street) by five unrelated fields, breaking the logical grouping of the address section and making the form harder to scan and fill in correctly.

findings.evidence: Fields present are House number, Street address, Postal code - no city/town field
findings.fix: Add a required "City" field adjacent to the street/postal fields.
findings.violation: A complete mailing address requires a city/town, but no such field exists anywhere in the form.

findings.fix: Merge "Overnight" and "Next-day" into one option, and move "International" to a separate destination/region control if it's needed at all.
findings.violation: "Overnight" and "Next-day" are effectively the same shipping speed and will confuse users choosing between them, and "International" is a destination category, not a shipping speed, so it doesn't belong in the same list.

findings.evidence: `<select id="shipspeed-select" required="">` and `<select id="hear-select" required="">`, both with no blank/placeholder first option
findings.fix: Add a disabled, selected-by-default placeholder option (e.g. "Select one") to both selects.
findings.violation: Because the first `<option>` is selected by default and there's no empty placeholder option, a user who never touches the dropdown will silently submit "Standard" / "Search engine" as if they had chosen it.

findings.evidence: `row-name`: `<label>Full name</label><input ... name="full_name" autocomplete="name">` vs `row-legalname`: `<label>Your name</label><input ... name="legal_name" autocomplete="name">`
findings.fix: Remove one of the duplicate name fields, or clearly differentiate their purpose (e.g. "Legal name for shipping documents" vs. display name) if both are genuinely needed.
findings.violation: The form asks for the user's name twice under different labels ("Full name" and "Your name"), both marked required with the same `autocomplete="name"`, which is redundant and will confuse browser autofill into filling both with the same value.

findings.fix: Remove the inline style and apply any needed font-size rule consistently via CSS to all inputs, or delete it if unnecessary.
findings.violation: This is the only input in the form with an inline style; singling it out suggests a leftover debugging/mobile-zoom fix rather than an intentional, consistent design choice.

findings.evidence: `<label id="contacttime-label" for="contacttime-input" style="display:block">Preferred contact time</label><input id="contacttime-input" name="contact_time" type="text" required="">`
findings.fix: Replace the text input with a `<select>` of time ranges (or paired start/end time inputs), and move the `display:block` styling into shared CSS instead of an inline style on one label.
findings.violation: "Preferred contact time" is a free-text field with no format guidance (e.g. "Weekdays 9 - 5"), so submitted values will be inconsistent and hard to process; the label also carries a one-off inline style not used elsewhere.

findings.evidence: `<button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button>` placed between row-contacttime and row-hear
findings.fix: Remove the button if unused, or give it a clear purpose/label and wire up its behavior if it's meant to do something.
findings.violation: This button has no associated handler, description, or context in the document - it's unclear what "details" it refers to, and it's the only element with this inline button styling, making it look like orphaned/leftover markup inside the signup form.

findings.evidence: Mix of fields like "Full name"/"Your name", "Membership number", "Account number", "Company website", "Organization name" all marked required in the same form
findings.fix: Split the form into clearly labeled sections (e.g. "Personal details," "Shipping address," "Business/membership details") using `<fieldset>`/`<legend>`, and reconsider which fields are actually required for a standard consumer account.
findings.violation: The form conflates a personal consumer signup (name, email, password, shipping address) with business/membership account fields (organization, company website, membership number, account number) without any visual or structural separation, making it unclear what kind of account is being created.
